sunday.themeNote: All four readings this week circle around one idea: God gives generously, even when we feel like we have nothing. Isaiah invites people who are empty-handed to come and be fed. The psalm says God opens his hand and satisfies every living thing. Paul insists that nothing in the universe can cut us off from God's love. And in the Gospel, Jesus takes a tiny amount of food and feeds thousands. Together, these passages ask us to consider where our real hunger comes from and who can actually fill it.

readings.label: First Reading
readings.fullText:
Thus says the LORD:
All you who are thirsty,
come to the water!
You who have no money,
come, receive grain and eat;
Come, without paying and without cost,
drink wine and milk!
Why spend your money for what is not bread;
your wages for what fails to satisfy?
Heed me, and you shall eat well,
you shall delight in rich fare.
Come to me heedfully,
listen, that you may have life.
I will renew with you the everlasting covenant,
the benefits assured to David.
readings.summary: God speaks through the prophet Isaiah and invites anyone who is thirsty or hungry to come and receive what they need, at no cost. He is not talking only about food and water. He is pointing to something deeper: a life that is truly satisfying, not just busy or full of things. God promises a lasting relationship with those who listen to him, the same faithful love he showed to King David long ago.

prompts.question: "Why spend your money for what is not bread; your wages for what fails to satisfy?" Think of one thing you keep reaching for lately when you feel stressed or empty. Does it actually leave you feeling better afterward?
prompts.starter: The thing I keep reaching for is… and honestly, after I do it I feel…

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.fullText:
R. (cf. 16) The hand of the Lord feeds us; he answers all our needs.
The LORD is gracious and merciful,
slow to anger and of great kindness.
The LORD is good to all
and compassionate toward all his works.
R. The hand of the Lord feeds us; he answers all our needs.
The eyes of all look hopefully to you,
and you give them their food in due season;
you open your hand
and satisfy the desire of every living thing.
R. The hand of the Lord feeds us; he answers all our needs.
The LORD is just in all his ways
and holy in all his works.
The LORD is near to all who call upon him,
to all who call upon him in truth.
R. The hand of the Lord feeds us; he answers all our needs.
readings.summary: This psalm is a song of praise that describes what God is like. God is kind, patient, and compassionate. He pays attention to every creature and provides what each one needs at the right time. The refrain sums it up simply: God feeds us and answers our needs.

prompts.question: "You open your hand and satisfy the desire of every living thing." Think of a moment this week, even a small one, when something you needed just showed up. What was that like?
prompts.starter: The moment that comes to mind is… and at the time I thought…

readings.label: Second Reading
readings.fullText:
Brothers and sisters:
What will separate us from the love of Christ?
Will anguish, or distress, or persecution, or famine,
or nakedness, or peril, or the sword?
No, in all these things we conquer overwhelmingly
through him who loved us.
For I am convinced that neither death, nor life,
nor angels, nor principalities,
nor present things, nor future things,
nor powers, nor height, nor depth,
nor any other creature will be able to separate us
from the love of God in Christ Jesus our Lord.
readings.summary: Paul is writing to early Christians who are going through real hardship, things like danger, hunger, and fear. He wants them to know that none of those hard things can break their connection to God's love. He lists every force he can think of, from death to angels to the future itself, and says not one of them is strong enough to separate us from that love.

prompts.question: "What will separate us from the love of Christ?" Paul lists real, painful things like danger, hunger, and fear. Which of those words describes something you are carrying right now?
prompts.starter: The word that stopped me was… because right now I am dealing with…

readings.label: Gospel
readings.fullText:
When Jesus heard of the death of John the Baptist,
he withdrew in a boat to a deserted place by himself.
The crowds heard of this and followed him on foot from their towns.
When he disembarked and saw the vast crowd,
his heart was moved with pity for them, and he cured their sick.
When it was evening, the disciples approached him and said,
“This is a deserted place and it is already late;
dismiss the crowds so that they can go to the villages
and buy food for themselves.”
Jesus said to them, “There is no need for them to go away;
give them some food yourselves.”
But they said to him,
“Five loaves and two fish are all we have here.”
Then he said, “Bring them here to me,”
and he ordered the crowds to sit down on the grass.
Taking the five loaves and the two fish, and looking up to heaven,
he said the blessing, broke the loaves,
and gave them to the disciples,
who in turn gave them to the crowds.
They all ate and were satisfied,
and they picked up the fragments left over—
twelve wicker baskets full.
Those who ate were about five thousand men,
not counting women and children.
readings.summary: Jesus has just heard that his cousin John has been killed. He tries to go somewhere quiet to be alone, but a large crowd follows him. Instead of turning them away, he feels deep compassion and heals the sick among them. When evening comes and the disciples worry about feeding everyone, Jesus takes five loaves of bread and two fish, gives thanks, and somehow feeds more than five thousand people, with food left over.

prompts.question: "Five loaves and two fish are all we have here." Think of a situation in your life right now where what you have feels nowhere near enough. What would it mean to hand that over instead of holding on to it?
prompts.starter: The situation I thought of is… and handing it over feels…

prompts.question: "His heart was moved with pity for them." Jesus had just gotten bad news and was trying to grieve alone, but he still stopped for the crowd. Is there someone in your life you have been too worn out to show up for lately?
prompts.starter: The person who came to mind is… and if I am honest, I have been…
